articles.summary: We’ve always been confident in our ability to build a strong agent for any one of those workflows. We do have a cracked engineering team, after all. The harder question was how to ensure our platform is truly functional at scale: we need to build hundreds of them, across different use cases and customers, without initiating a new software project. What we needed was a repeatable way to transform our customers’ workflow into an agent that meets their standard. That is what Builder is.
articles.title: How Bretton’s agent builder actually works

articles.summary: We completely rebuilt our architecture three times since starting Bretton due to the rapid advancement of AI technology. Every generation described here ran in production inside financial institutions, carrying real cases under real controls. Each move took a different kind of complexity out of code and put it in the right layer of the system. Learn how we did it and what changed.
articles.title: The importance of architectural reinvention for financial services AI

articles.summary: MVB, a subsidiary of MVB Financial Corp. (Nasdaq: MVBF), has selected Bretton AI to deliver AI-native Managed Services for its back-office operations. A dedicated US-based Bretton AI team will run Anti-Money Laundering transaction monitoring and Know Your Customer work, delivered as completed alerts and cases, in line with MVB's policies and risk framework.
articles.title: MVB Bank is scaling its Fintech business without scaling its back office

articles.summary: This post showcases how Bretton AI validates AI agents before and after they go into production with an anonymized customer example. It covers our model risk framework, the scenario testing protocol we ran against a real production dataset, the fairness analysis we conducted across 129 countries and multiple identity field types, and, most importantly, the gaps we found and what we are doing about them.
articles.title: Moving an agent to production

articles.summary: The foundation models work great and will keep getting better. So why do most agent projects in financial services still fail? And fail in the same, predictable way? For those who have tried, it becomes quickly apparent that there’s a vast distance between a demo that impresses a room and a system an institution can rely on, at production volume, inside its own controls. That distance is where the build-versus-buy conundrum is almost always underestimated.
articles.title: Building an agent was never the hard part: the build-vs-buy conundrum
